title: test(plugin-auth): the forced-reset OAuth test stamps its grant one whole second ahead and turns red when the call takes longer
body:
security#2 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcW9L8Noz9BxEwjwiov

**Where:** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts:530-538`, in the test "an administrator's forced reset ends them too and reports the apps; with revocation off it ends none".

**Seen:** merge-queue build [44999732595](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/44999732595), Test Core (10/10), with PR #36127 in the group (that PR touches only `objectql`):

```
src/password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts:538  expect(await grantStands()).toBe(true)
AssertionError: expected false to be true
```

**Why it goes red under load:** the test takes `issuedAt = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 1` (whole seconds, at most one second ahead), and `grantStands()` calls `mcpConsentAdmits` without a millisecond claim. On a consent row, a token with no millisecond claim is placed at `issuedAt * 1000`. The routine reset in between writes the credential-change time. If more than about one second passes between taking `issuedAt` and that reset (the admin HTTP call under the full-suite load), the change time lands after `issuedAt * 1000`, and the grant reads as issued before the change. The product rule is unchanged. The test's premise, that the reset happens within the same second, is what fails.

**Fix direction (test-only):** read the credential-change time after the routine reset and derive `issuedAt` from it, or pass a millisecond claim later than it. Either way the assertion no longer depends on wall-clock time. Keep the forced-reset half as it is.

**Not a regression** of the PR in that group. One queue build so far; filed so the next red lands on a known card.
